name: nesc
desc: Programming language for deeply networked systems
why: A nesC language for TinyOS sensor networks is a strange, old-school concurrency dialect, though deprecated and dormant.

brief.what_it_is: nesC is an extension to the C programming language, pronounced "NES-see", that the README says is designed to embody the structuring concepts and execution model of TinyOS. TinyOS is described as an event-driven operating system for sensor network nodes with very limited resources. The project ships a compiler driver set (nescc, nescc-mig, nescc-ncg, nescc-wiring), and the README's usage section points to the nescc man page. The README does not spell out inputs and outputs beyond this, so treat the rest as unverified. The Homebrew description calls it a programming language for deeply networked systems, which is broader than the README's TinyOS framing.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames nesC as a way to express TinyOS's structuring concepts and event-driven execution model directly in the language, for sensor nodes with tiny memory (its example is 8K bytes of program memory and 512 bytes of RAM).

The README's usage pointer: read the nescc man page for how to use the compiler.

brief.install_notes: Building from source needs automake, autoconf (2.64 or 2.69 or later; the README says 2.67 and 2.68 are known not to work), emacs (not version 24.3), gperf, bison and flex. The install sequence is ./Bootstrap, ./configure, make, make install. No hardware, accounts or runtime configuration are mentioned in the README. The README does not describe a first-run step.
brief.standout: It is an old-school C extension that bakes TinyOS's event-driven, component-wiring model into the language itself, aimed at severely memory-constrained sensor nodes rather than general networked applications.
brief.status: Archived. The GitHub releases page shows the banner "This repository was archived by the owner on Apr 12, 2026. It is now read-only." The latest listed release is v1.3.6 ("version 1.3.6 nesc compiler"), marked Pre-release, posted 07 Aug with no year shown in the page text. The scout note calls it deprecated and dormant. The archive banner supports dormant, but the README itself does not say deprecated.
brief.caveats: The repository is archived and read-only, so no fixes are coming from upstream. Build requirements are picky: specific autoconf versions, an emacs version that excludes 24.3, and several parser and lexer tools. The README is short and points to a man page for usage, with no tutorial or examples. The 1.3.6 release notes mention Mac OS X alignment support and emacs compatibility, so the compiler has been built on macOS. The README does not state a license, so check the repository before reuse.
quotes: nesC (pronounced "NES-see") is an extension to the C programming language designed to embody the structuring concepts and execution model of TinyOS.
TinyOS is an event-driven operating system designed for sensor network nodes that have very limited resources (e.g., 8K bytes of program memory, 512 bytes of RAM).
